scope: An implementation-bound reference for one GitHub organization/repository first, then a reusable distribution. It covers issue intake, readiness, durable claiming, isolated implementation, independent verification, PR/review/merge, Project v2 projection, release/canary/rollback hooks, operations, and governed workflow improvement. Git is authoritative for desired policy, schemas, workflows, prompts, eval definitions, and protected runbooks; a durable control-plane database is authoritative for event order, leases, approvals, attempts, and actual lifecycle state; GitHub Issues/PRs/Checks/Project v2 are user-facing resources and materialized views. It does not claim safe autonomous product prioritization, general incident repair, policy self-modification, or unattended high-risk production change. Project v2 remote values are actual mutable remote state, not magically made declarative by committing YAML; the reconciler explicitly observes, compares, acts, and reports drift (GitHub GraphQL Projects API: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/using-the-api-to-manage-projects).
current_capabilities: GitHub supports YAML issue forms, GitHub App webhook/API identities, Project v2 fields/items through GraphQL, repository rulesets, required reviews/status checks, merge queues, protected deployment environments, reusable Actions workflows, OIDC, artifact attestations, audit logs, and API/webhook delivery inspection. Project item/field mutations require node IDs discovered at runtime; `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` supports a single field value per call and supports text, number, date, single-select or iteration values, so reconciliation is neither an atomic whole-project transaction nor a Git apply (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updateprojectv2itemfieldvalue). Actions `concurrency` permits at most one running and one pending job/workflow per group and ordering is not guaranteed, so it is not a durable FIFO lease service (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/using-concurrency). GitHub recommends webhook receivers answer within 10 seconds, validate signatures, use delivery IDs, process asynchronously, and cache/redeliver failed deliveries; therefore a database inbox/outbox remains required (https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks). Installation access tokens expire after one hour and can be narrowed to repositories and permissions (https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app). GitHub is a capable integration surface, not a complete durable orchestrator or safety case.
representative_systems: Reference components and transferable patterns: GitHub Projects v2/Issues/PRs/Rulesets/Actions/Environments as collaboration and enforcement surfaces; a GitHub App as the machine identity; PostgreSQL as transactional event/inbox/outbox, aggregate, lease, and fencing store; an OCI container or ephemeral VM per attempt; GitHub-hosted Actions or ephemeral self-hosted runners as clean verifier identities; OpenTelemetry plus W3C Trace Context for correlation; Sigstore/SLSA-style provenance and GitHub artifact attestations for evidence; CloudEvents 1.0 as an event-envelope influence; and Argo Rollouts (optional, not MVP) for metric-gated canary/abort. GitHub Spec Kit is a useful spec artifact pattern but not outcome evidence (https://github.com/github/spec-kit). Durable-execution products may replace the PostgreSQL worker later, but the contract must not depend on vendor magic.
primary_evidence: Primary-source basis: GitHub documents Project v2 GraphQL automation and mutations (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/using-the-api-to-manage-projects; https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updateprojectv2itemfieldvalue), issue-form syntax (https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema), GitHub App tokens (https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app), webhook security/operations (https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries; https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks), rulesets (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules), merge queues and their `merge_group` CI trigger (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#merge_group), secure Actions use and OIDC (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/openid-connect), environments (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments), and artifact attestations (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/using-artifact-attestations). CloudEvents defines common required context attributes (https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md); W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry define interoperable correlation/telemetry (https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/; https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/overview/); SLSA defines provenance levels and threats (https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/levels).
independent_evidence: Challenge evidence limits autonomy. OWASP treats prompt injection and excessive agency as architectural risks, supporting capability enforcement outside prompts (https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/; https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/). The OpenSSF Scorecard project checks branch protection, pinned dependencies, token permissions, dangerous workflows and other controls, illustrating that repository automation expands the attack surface (https://github.com/ossf/scorecard). GitHub Security Lab shows why `pull_request_target` plus untrusted checkout can become a 'pwn request' and leak write tokens/secrets (https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/). NIST SSDF calls for protected development environments, provenance, review, and response rather than trusting a generating tool (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final). SWE-bench Live finds material difficulty and contamination/recency issues in coding-agent evaluation, so benchmark success does not establish safe repository ownership (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23419). These sources contradict any claim that a capable coding model plus green self-authored tests is an adequate authorization boundary.
metrics_and_limits: Platform facts: installation tokens normally expire in 1 hour; Actions concurrency is only one running plus one pending member per key and has arbitrary order; webhook receivers should return 2xx within 10 seconds; Project GraphQL mutations update one field at a time; GraphQL is cost/rate limited and exposes rate-limit status (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/rate-limits-and-query-limits-for-the-graphql-api). Treat published GitHub limits as deployment-time inputs, not hard-coded constants, because plan and product limits can change (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/limits-for-projects). MVP local budgets: one active lease per work item; lease TTL 15 minutes, heartbeat every 60 seconds, fencing token on every write; at most 2 repair attempts; one repository/branch/PR per attempt; wall-clock, token, command, diff-size, egress, and spend caps in policy. These are starting values, not evidence-backed universal optima. Measure webhook ingest lag p95/p99, duplicate rate, reconciliation lag, drift age, lease steals, retries, blocked reasons, CI duration/flakiness, review edits/rejections, merge lead time, escaped defects, rollback rate/time, cost per accepted change, and policy denials. Always report numerator, denominator, task/risk mix, observation window, and baseline.
recommended_design: Use a small deterministic control plane around an untrusted planner/implementer. Components: (1) GitHub App webhook ingress verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256`, stores raw delivery by `(installation_id, delivery_id)`, returns quickly; (2) PostgreSQL tables `inbox`, `events`, `work_items`, `commands`, `leases`, `approvals`, `attempts`, `evidence`, `outbox`, and `github_projection`; (3) transactional controller validates transitions/policy, assigns monotonically increasing aggregate versions and fencing tokens, and writes outbox rows; (4) reconciler applies managed desired schema to GitHub and projects actual lifecycle state to issue/Project/Checks with read-after-write; (5) planner is read-only; (6) implementation worker gets a fresh sandbox and scoped short-lived credential, never approval/merge/deploy rights; (7) clean verifier runs from exact candidate SHA under a separate identity; (8) publisher opens/updates the PR; rulesets/merge queue/environments enforce protected transitions; (9) immutable evidence/object storage and OpenTelemetry preserve audit/correlation. Start with PostgreSQL `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; adopt a workflow engine only after measured scale/recovery need. Keep all LLM outputs proposals until deterministic validation and the risk-specific gate.
state_and_event_contract: Aggregate states: `INBOX -> TRIAGED -> PLANNING <-> CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED -> READY_REVIEW -> READY -> LEASED -> EXECUTING -> PROPOSED -> VERIFYING -> REVIEW_REQUIRED -> MERGE_READY -> MERGED -> RELEASE_READY -> CANARY -> {DEPLOYED,ROLLED_BACK,HUMAN_INCIDENT} -> {VERIFIED,LEARN} -> CLOSED`, with `REJECTED`, `DEFERRED`, and `BLOCKED` explicit. Only the controller appends transitions. Every event envelope has `event_id(UUID)`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `source`, `subject=work_item_id`, `occurred_at`, `received_at`, `actor_principal`, `correlation_id`, `causation_id`, `github_delivery_id?`, `aggregate_version`, `spec_hash?`, `policy_version`, `payload_digest`, and typed `data`; follow CloudEvents naming concepts without falsely claiming wire conformance (https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md). A command has `command_id`, caller, expected aggregate version, idempotency key, deadline, policy decision and result. Duplicate delivery/command returns the recorded outcome; out-of-order facts are recorded but cannot regress state. Lease is `(work_item,attempt,holder,expires_at,fencing_token,heartbeat_at)`; takeover increments the token and all stale-token commits fail. Approval is `(work_item,spec_hash,candidate_sha_or_artifact_digest,policy_version,scope,approver,approved_at,expires_at)` and any bound-input change invalidates it. Evidence binds verifier identity/image digest/base SHA/head SHA/test manifest/results/provenance. The GitHub projection records remote node IDs, last observed value/update time, last applied aggregate version, and digest. Webhooks wake reconciliation; scheduled scans repair missed delivery. Desired configuration manages field/option/ruleset definitions; controller events manage item lifecycle. Human remote changes are accepted only as authenticated commands allowed by policy; unknown/conflicting changes become drift incidents. Because multi-field Project mutations are not atomic, write in deterministic order, checkpoint each field, read back, retry with idempotent desired values, and show `SYNC_ERROR` rather than pretending success.
repository_artifacts: Minimum tree: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/work-item.yml`; `.github/workflows/agent-intake.yml`, `agent-verify.yml`, `merge-queue.yml`, `release.yml`, `reconcile.yml`; `.github/dependabot.yml`; `CODEOWNERS`; `agent-os/project.schema.yaml` (managed Project fields/options and ownership mode, never remote IDs); `agent-os/states.yaml` (states, transitions, terminal states); `agent-os/policy.rego` or equivalent deterministic policy plus `policy-tests/`; `agent-os/risk-tiers.yaml`; `agent-os/capability-profiles/*.yaml`; `agent-os/definition-of-ready.yaml`; `agent-os/events/*.schema.json`; `agent-os/spec.schema.json`; `agent-os/evidence.schema.json`; `agent-os/agents/AGENTS.md` and role-specific instructions; `agent-os/evals/cases/*.yaml`, frozen fixtures and score thresholds; `agent-os/runbooks/{webhook-replay,project-drift,stale-lease,token-revoke,queue-backlog,rollback,kill-switch}.md`; `agent-os/migrations/`; `agent-os/VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md`; `docs/agent-os/architecture.md`, `threat-model.md`, `approval-matrix.md`, `rollout.md`. Store a generated `project-lock.json` containing observed GitHub node IDs only as a non-authoritative cache or encrypted deployment artifact; never review it as desired status. Pin reusable workflows/actions to immutable commit SHAs, declare minimal `permissions`, and validate schemas/policy in PR CI (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions).
workflow_steps: Scenario A—bounded bug: verified webhook -> normalize/dedupe -> issue-form validation -> planner produces spec, failing-base regression, plan, risk and rollback -> owner approval binds spec hash -> controller leases -> ephemeral worker patches branch -> clean verifier proves base-fail/candidate-pass and all required checks -> publisher creates draft PR/evidence check -> independent review binds current SHA -> merge queue tests `merge_group` head -> immutable artifact/attestation -> low-risk canary -> verify -> learn/close. Scenario B—ambiguity: missing product choice causes `CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED`, lease absent/revoked, bounded question posted, and no production PR until revised spec is approved. Scenario C—CI repair: dedupe by workflow/run/job/head/fingerprint; rerun one known transient or allow at most two same-scope repair attempts; security/policy/unknown/repeated failure stops `BLOCKED`. Scenario D—worker death: missed heartbeat expires lease; new attempt gets a higher fence; late old worker cannot publish. Scenario E—Project drift: poll observes manual option rename/value conflict; non-destructive managed schema repair may be planned/applied, but destructive change or lifecycle disagreement creates `SYNC_ERROR`/human review; Git never overwrites actual work state silently. Scenario F—improvement: outcome becomes sanitized eval case -> agent drafts prompt/tool/policy proposal -> separate curator approves corpus -> offline and shadow run -> human approves exact version -> limited canary -> rollback on threshold; proposer cannot edit hidden tests, lower gates, approve, or promote. Stop on scope/permission expansion, head/spec/policy drift, budget expiry, flaky oracle, unavailable rollback, or uncertainty above configured threshold.
human_gates: Human approval is mandatory for product intent/priority, unresolved ambiguity, the initial READY decision during pilot, all R2/R3 work, auth/crypto/IAM/privacy/payments/destructive migration/public API/CI-policy/CODEOWNERS/ruleset changes, new registries or credentials, flaky or missing oracle, production release beyond a proven R0/R1 profile, inconclusive canary, failed rollback, exceptions, and promotion of self-improvement. R0 mechanical and later proven R1 profiles may advance conditionally only after staged evidence. Required approval is a signed/audited record bound to `work_item_id + spec_hash + exact head SHA/artifact digest + policy version + capability profile + scope + expiry`; a new commit or relevant policy/spec change invalidates it. CODEOWNERS and rulesets enforce named independent review, but repository administrators/bypass actors must be minimized and audited (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules). The planner/implementer may recommend a risk tier but cannot de-escalate it; the improvement proposer cannot curate its holdout, approve policy, or promote itself.
security_and_failure_modes: Threats and controls: forged/replayed webhook -> HMAC over raw body, delivery-ID uniqueness, timestamp/installation checks, append-only raw record; prompt injection in issue/code/log -> treat text as data, deterministic tool policy, deny-by-default egress, no ambient secrets; token theft/excessive agency -> short-lived narrowed GitHub App/OIDC identity, separate planner/worker/verifier/publisher/release principals, branch/path/verb/budget bounds; malicious Actions/dependency -> immutable SHA pin, dependency review, Scorecard, restricted untrusted workflow and no secret-bearing `pull_request_target` checkout; self-authored weak tests -> protected/frozen tests, base-fail/candidate-pass, clean verifier and human semantic review; race/duplicate/out-of-order -> inbox idempotency, aggregate compare-and-swap, fenced leases, transactional outbox; lost webhook/API outage/rate limit -> exponential jitter, `Retry-After`/rate-limit awareness, dead-letter queue, scheduled inventory reconciliation; Project partial write/manual drift -> checkpoints, read-back, ownership rules, visible sync error, no destructive auto-repair; force-push/head drift -> bind evidence/approval to SHA and reverify; stale worker -> fence all publishes; runaway retries/cost -> hard attempt/time/token/spend limits and circuit breaker; artifact/log tampering -> digest, attestation, immutable retention and audit export; compromised control plane -> kill switch revokes installation tokens, disables workers/reconciler writes, freezes queues and preserves evidence. GitHub warns untrusted Action input and compromised third-party Actions can expose credentials (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions).
validation_and_tests: CI must include: JSON Schema positive/negative fixtures for every event/spec/evidence version and compatibility/migration tests; table-driven transition/role/risk rules; property/model tests that no path reaches READY without a matching approval, no stale fence publishes, terminal states do not regress, and implementer never approves/merges/deploys; policy tests for every capability and bypass; GitHub recorded-contract fixtures plus periodic sandbox-organization integration tests for issue forms, Project nodes/fields, rulesets, check runs, `merge_group`, environment approval and token scopes; replay tests for duplicate, out-of-order, delayed and missing webhooks; transactional fault injection between event/outbox/API/checkpoint commits; rate-limit/5xx/timeout chaos; concurrent claim/heartbeat/expiry tests; clean-room base-fail/candidate-pass E2E; adversarial prompt/tool/egress/secret tests; malicious fork/`pull_request_target` negative tests; Project manual-edit/rename/delete/partial-mutation reconciliation tests; approval invalidation after SHA/spec/policy change; backup restore, kill switch, token revocation and webhook replay drills; canary PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE and rollback-failure simulations; eval contamination/access tests and proposer-curator-promoter separation. Block rollout on any privilege-negative test failure, event loss, stale-fence success, false approval, or unverifiable evidence.
operational_maintenance: Runbooks must name owner, trigger, preconditions, bounded commands, validation, compensator, escalation and evidence location. Daily: reconcile open work/PR/check/project projections, inspect dead letters and expiring tokens/leases. Weekly: sample accepted agent changes, review denials/retries/flakes/cost and clean expired sandboxes/branches/artifacts under retention policy. Monthly: restore backup in isolation, replay an event partition, test kill switch/token revocation, review App permissions/egress/action pins/ruleset bypass and Project drift. Quarterly or on model/tool/policy upgrade: rerun frozen and fresh evals, threat model, disaster/rollback drill, schema migration rehearsal and human approval. Upgrade with expand/migrate/contract schemas, dual-read/shadow where needed, immutable versioned policy/prompts/images, canary controller instance, and rollback. Webhook recovery reads the durable inbox first, uses GitHub redelivery where available, then performs inventory reconciliation; never infer absence from one missing event (https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/testing-and-troubleshooting-webhooks/redelivering-webhooks). Export GitHub audit log and controller audit records to a separately controlled sink (https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/keeping-your-organization-secure/managing-security-settings-for-your-organization/managing-the-audit-log-for-your-organization).
maturity_and_uncertainty: Mature: GitHub protection primitives, App authentication, webhook HMAC, CI, issue forms, PostgreSQL transactions, OIDC, telemetry standards and review gates. Conditional but implementable: reliable Project v2 reconciliation, bounded R0/R1 proposal automation, repair loops and canary promotion; these need repository-specific pilots, because Project mutations are partial and remote humans can edit state. Experimental: model-based planning/triage, semantic verification, automatic risk classification, observability RCA and improvement proposals. Unsupported as a safety claim: general unattended issue-to-production operation, novel incident repair, irreversible migration, or any mechanism where the agent changes/approves its own permission, policy, evaluator or promotion threshold. No external study supplies a universal safe error rate or ROI for this full architecture. GitHub API fields, limits, plans and agent features may change by the requested as-of date; deployment must regenerate an API/schema/permissions compatibility report.
implementation_recommendation: Stage 0 (2–4 weeks): commit schemas/policy/runbooks, GitHub App read-only, webhook inbox/event store, shadow state machine and Project drift report. Exit: 14 consecutive days with zero unexplained lost deliveries in reconciled inventory, 100% duplicate replays idempotent, restoration/replay drill passes, and no writes. Stage 1: assistive planning/draft checks only; humans approve and execute. Exit after >=30 representative tickets: 100% READY records trace criteria to tests/owners/rollback, no unauthorized tool call succeeds, reviewers rate evidence useful on >=80% (predefine rubric), and false/block rates are reported. Stage 2: agent creates branches/draft PRs for allowlisted R0/R1; separate clean verifier, no auto-merge/deploy. Exit after >=50 accepted/closed attempts and >=30 days: zero privilege escapes or stale-fence publishes, every candidate reproducible from SHA, escaped-defect rate is not worse than matched human baseline within a predeclared non-inferiority margin, and median review/lead time or cost improves without worse severity mix. Stage 3: conditional auto-merge for one R0 profile, merge queue, automatic low-risk canary rollback; human sample >=10%. Exit after >=100 eligible changes and >=60 days: all rule predicates met at current head, 100% rollback drills pass, no high-severity escape, SLO/error-budget guardrails remain within predeclared bounds. Stage 4: expand one capability/risk/repository at a time. Never graduate on volume alone; any privilege escape, false approval, high-severity defect, evidence tampering or rollback failure freezes expansion and triggers review. Prefer this thin auditable controller over an all-purpose autonomous agent framework.

conflicts: (1) GitHub Projects looks like 'status as code,' but official APIs expose mutable remote objects and one-field mutations; resolution: Git declares desired schema/policy while observed remote item values and durable controller events remain explicit actual state. (2) Actions concurrency sounds like a lock/queue, but GitHub states only one running/one pending and arbitrary order; resolution: use it only to suppress duplicate workflows, not for ownership, FIFO or fencing. (3) Project built-in automation may move items, while the controller also projects state; resolution: disable overlapping writers or mark each field as controller-owned, human-owned or imported and alert on conflict. (4) artifact attestation proves provenance/identity, not functional correctness or authorization; keep independent tests, review and policy. (5) CODEOWNERS/rulesets protect branches but bypass/admin paths and configuration ownership vary by plan/repository; inventory effective enforcement and test it. (6) agent benchmarks/product docs show coding utility, while OWASP, Security Lab, SSDF and SWE-bench Live show prompt, workflow and evaluation limits; resolution: agent output is a proposal and deterministic/human controls own consequence. (7) automatic Project drift repair improves consistency but can erase legitimate human action; only safe, non-destructive schema convergence is automatic, while semantic/item conflicts require review.
confidence: Overall: high for the architecture boundary, GitHub primitives, webhook/inbox/outbox, separate identities, SHA-bound approvals, fenced leases, clean verification and staged rollout logic; medium for exact Project v2 reconciliation behavior and organization-plan enforcement because API schema, limits and plan features change; medium-low for proposed numeric pilot thresholds because they are explicit local decision gates, not externally validated universal constants; low for productivity/defect improvement until the target repository supplies matched baselines. Claim-level rule: platform statements cite official docs; security challenges cite OWASP/NIST/OpenSSF/Security Lab; agent capability limits cite research. Deployment confidence requires a live sandbox compatibility test on the target GitHub plan and API schema.
uncertain: The requested as-of date is 2026-09-13. GitHub documentation is continuously updated and often has no stable publication date; re-check live GraphQL schema, webhook payloads, ruleset/environment availability, App permission names, plan restrictions and limits immediately before rollout.

GitHub does not provide an atomic declarative transaction over an entire Project v2. Exact conflict detection semantics and `updatedAt` coverage should be verified in a sandbox; the design therefore assumes single controller writer, checkpoint/read-back and visible drift rather than optimistic atomicity.
Webhook coverage for every relevant Project v2 manual edit may be incomplete or evolve. Scheduled GraphQL inventory scans are required; measure reconciliation lag and missed-event rate.

The 15-minute lease, 60-second heartbeat, two repair attempts and rollout sample sizes/thresholds are proposed safe starting policies, not universal evidence-backed constants. Tune only through governed pilots.
No evidence found proves end-to-end unattended issue-to-production operation is safe across task classes. R2/R3 and policy/self-improvement promotion remain human-gated.
